profile.org_note: Not a conventional homebuilder: HFHI is a 501(c)(3) umbrella (FY ends June 30; legal address Americus, GA; administrative HQ Atlanta) that supports independent, separately incorporated local affiliates, which buy the land, build the homes and hold the mortgages. HFHI itself has no land or division-president structure. The people who matter for land capital are the Chief Financial and Administration Officer (oversees Finance and Habitat Capital) and the head of Habitat Capital, the wholly owned CDFI that lends to affiliates for land acquisition, predevelopment and construction and runs the US Property Acquisition Fund; the SVP U.S. Office and Canada leads affiliate support.
profile.summary: Nonprofit, not a for-sale homebuilder: the Builder 100 closings are the combined output of independent local Habitat affiliates in all 50 states, each of which manages its own home-building, sources its own land and sells to lower-income buyers on affordable mortgages. HFHI in Atlanta is the support and funding hub (FY2026 revenue $393.7M, total assets $767.3M) and finances affiliates' land through its CDFI, Habitat Capital ($46.8M lent to 31 affiliates in 20 states in FY2026), and the $82.5M US Property Acquisition Fund managed by Enterprise Community Loan Fund. It is not a plausible lot-option / land-banking customer in the conventional sense: there is no central land buyer, no takedown schedule, and its land capital is concessionary (2% to 6% notes from banks and foundations).
